There is a new on-demand plugin install capability: running `entire graph` when the `entire-graph` plugin is not installed offers (interactively, on a TTY) to download and install the plugin. On unix it works; on Windows the download lands but the resulting `entire-graph` binary ends up EMPTY/broken.

Find and report, with file paths and line numbers and code excerpts:
1. All files implementing plugin install/download: look for `plugin_store.go`, `plugin_index`, `pluginRoot`, `pluginParentDir`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`, `installPlugin`, `downloadPlugin`, archive extraction (tar.gz / zip), checksum verification, `os.Rename`, `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn`, `osroot.WriteFile`, `CreateTempIn`, in cmd/entire/cli/*.go and cmd/entire/main.go and internal/.
2. Trace the full code path from `entire graph` (external command resolution in cmd/entire/main.go, `entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) to the install prompt, download, extraction, writing of the binary into the plugin `bin` directory, and making it executable. Include exactly how the destination filename is computed on Windows (`.exe` suffix?), how the archive asset name is chosen per GOOS/GOARCH (windows_arm64? amd64?), how the file is written (which os.Root / osroot APIs), whether a temp file + rename is used, whether the file is closed before rename, whether `syscall.Chmod` or `os.Chmod` is used, and any `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` branches.
3. How the downloaded asset is selected from a release index / manifest (is there a plugin index JSON or a git clone of an index repo? what does the manifest look like? is there a testdata example?). Check for GitHub release asset naming like `entire-graph_windows_arm64.zip` vs `.tar.gz`, and how zip vs tar.gz is decided.
4. Any existing tests for plugin install, especially with Windows-specific behavior or `_windows_test.go` files.
5. docs/architecture/external-commands.md contents relevant to plugin install.

Report exact code excerpts of the writing/extraction function(s) so the caller can reason about the Windows failure without re-reading everything.

51	// attacker who can rewrite one can rewrite both, and checksum verification

55	// keep working — traffic that never leaves the machine has no network
56	// attacker to defend against.

58		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)

61		}

372			return path.Base(u.Path)

375		if i := strings.IndexAny(trimmed, "?#"); i >= 0 {
376			trimmed = trimmed[:i]
377		}

408	// fetchAndVerify downloads rawURL into stagingDir, streaming the SHA-256 as
409	// it writes. A non-empty wantDigest is enforced; an empty one records the
410	// computed digest. 404/410 map to errAssetNotFound. Partial files are
411	// removed on verification failure so a hostile or truncated download never
412	// lingers in staging.
413	// Note on credentials: rawURL may carry userinfo, because releaseAssetBaseURL
414	// derives the asset URL from the repo URL and url.String() re-serializes it.
415	// The request keeps it — that is how the download authenticates to a private
416	// forge — but every message below goes through redactURL, since main.go prints
417	// command errors to stderr and a download failure is an ordinary event
418	// (network hiccup, 5xx, checksum mismatch), not an exceptional one.
419	func fetchAndVerify(ctx context.Context, rawURL, asset, wantDigest, stagingDir string) (*fetchedAsset, error) {
420		stagingRoot, err := osroot.Shared(stagingDir)
421		if err != nil {
422			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open staging dir: %w", err)
423		}
424	
425		// The asset name is normally one of our own candidates, but the
426		// single-URL download_url template path derives it from the URL and a
427		// future caller could pass a name straight from a remote manifest.
428		// Refuse anything that wouldn't stay inside stagingDir. Backslash is
429		// rejected on every platform — it's a separator on Windows, and a
430		// literal backslash in an asset name is never legitimate.
431		if asset == "" || asset == "." || asset == ".." ||
432			strings.ContainsAny(asset, `/\`) || asset != filepath.Base(asset) {
433			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsafe release asset name %q", asset)
434		}
435		if err := requireSecureAssetURL(rawURL); err != nil {
436			return nil, err
437		}
438		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, rawURL, nil)
439		if err != nil {
440			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build request for %s: %w", redactURL(rawURL), err)
441		}
442		resp, err := pluginHTTPClient.Do(req)
443		if err != nil {
444			return nil, fmt.Errorf("download %s: %w", redactURL(rawURL), err)
445		}
446		defer resp.Body.Close()
447		switch resp.StatusCode {
448		case http.StatusOK:
449		case http.StatusNotFound, http.StatusGone:
450			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: GET %s: %s", errAssetNotFound, redactURL(rawURL), resp.Status)
451		default:
452			return nil, fmt.Errorf("download %s: %s", redactURL(rawURL), resp.Status)
453		}
454	
455		// Through the staging root, with the asset as a name inside it. asset comes
456		// from assetCandidates today — selectAssetFromChecksums uses the downloaded
457		// manifest only as a membership test, so a remote name never reaches here —
458		// and assetNameFromURL runs path.Base. The root is what keeps that true if
459		// either of those ever starts trusting the manifest's spelling.
460		out, err := stagingRoot.Create(asset)
461		if err != nil {
462			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create staging file: %w", err)
463		}
464		dest := filepath.Join(stagingDir, asset)
465		h := sha256.New()
466		n, err := io.Copy(io.MultiWriter(out, h), io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxPluginAssetSize+1))
467		closeErr := out.Close()
468		if err != nil {
469			_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(stagingRoot, asset) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup of a staging file we are already abandoning
470			return nil, fmt.Errorf("download %s: %w", redactURL(rawURL), err)
471		}
472		if closeErr != nil {
473			_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(stagingRoot, asset) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup of a staging file we are already abandoning
474			return nil, fmt.Errorf("write staging file: %w", closeErr)
475		}
476		if n > maxPluginAssetSize {
477			_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(stagingRoot, asset) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup of a staging file we are already abandoning
478			return nil, fmt.Errorf("download %s: exceeds %d byte limit", redactURL(rawURL), int64(maxPluginAssetSize))
479		}
480		got := hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
481		if wantDigest != "" && !strings.EqualFold(got, wantDigest) {
482			_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(stagingRoot, asset) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup of a staging file we are already abandoning
483			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checksum mismatch for %s: got %s, want %s", asset, got, wantDigest)
484		}
485		return &fetchedAsset{Path: dest, Asset: asset, SHA256: got, Verified: wantDigest != ""}, nil
486	}

488	// extractPluginBinary locates the plugin executable inside the downloaded
489	// asset and writes it to destPath (mode 0755 on Unix). Raw binaries are
490	// copied; .tar.gz/.tgz and .zip archives are searched for an entry whose
491	// basename matches entire-<name>[.exe], wherever it sits in the archive.
492	func extractPluginBinary(assetPath, name string, destRoot *os.Root, destName string) error {
493		binName := pluginBinaryPrefix + name
494		lower := strings.ToLower(assetPath)
495		switch {
496		case strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".tar.gz") || strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".tgz"):
497			return extractFromTarGz(assetPath, binName, destRoot, destName)
498		case strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".zip"):
499			return extractFromZip(assetPath, binName, destRoot, destName)
500		default:
501			src, err := os.Open(assetPath) //nolint:gosec // staging-dir file we just wrote
502			if err != nil {
503				return fmt.Errorf("open asset: %w", err)
504			}
505			defer src.Close()
506			return writeExecutable(destRoot, destName, src)
507		}
508	}

511	// plugin binary, tolerating a Windows extension.
512	func matchesPluginBinary(entryName, binName string) bool {
513		base := path.Base(filepath.ToSlash(entryName))
514		if base == binName {
515			return true
516		}
517		return runtime.GOOS == windowsGOOS && strings.EqualFold(base, binName+windowsExeExt)

520	// safeArchiveEntry rejects entry names that could escape an extraction
521	// root. We only ever extract a single matched file to a fixed dest, so this
522	// is defense in depth against a hostile archive masking as a plugin.
523	func safeArchiveEntry(entryName string) bool {
524		clean := archiveEntryPath(entryName)
525		return !strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") && !path.IsAbs(clean) && !strings.Contains(entryName, "\x00")
526	}

528	// preferredArchiveEntry picks among entries whose basename matches the plugin
529	// binary. Shallowest path wins, then lexicographic order.
530	//
531	// Selection has to be deterministic and independent of archive order. Matching
532	// is by basename, so an archive can legitimately hold more than one candidate —
533	// goreleaser writes the binary at the root by default but nests it under a
534	// versioned directory with wrap_in_directory, and archives also ship things like
535	// completions/entire-<name>. Taking whichever came first meant the installed
536	// binary depended on the order the author's tar happened to be built in.
537	//
538	// Shallowest-first encodes the convention: the real binary sits at the root, or
539	// at worst one directory down; a same-named file deeper in the tree is a
540	// completion script or a doc, not the command.
541	func preferredArchiveEntry(names []string, binName string) string {
542		p := archiveEntryPicker{binName: binName}
543		for _, name := range names {
544			p.consider(name)
545		}
546		return p.best
547	}

549	// archiveEntryPicker keeps only the best candidate seen so far, so an archive
550	// can be scanned without materializing every entry name.
551	//
552	// That matters because the entry list is remote-controlled and the only prior
553	// check on it is that the asset's sha256 matched what the release published.
554	// Entry headers compress extremely well, so the 512 MiB maxPluginAssetSize
555	// admits tens of millions of them — enough that collecting the names would
556	// cost gigabytes of heap to end up choosing between the one or two entries a
557	// real release actually contains. A running minimum costs one string.
558	type archiveEntryPicker struct {
559		binName string
560		best    string
561		depth   int
562	}
563	
564	func (p *archiveEntryPicker) consider(name string) {
565		if !safeArchiveEntry(name) || !matchesPluginBinary(name, p.binName) {
566			return
567		}
568		clean := archiveEntryPath(name)
569		depth := strings.Count(clean, "/")
570		if p.best == "" || depth < p.depth || (depth == p.depth && clean < p.best) {
571			p.best, p.depth = clean, depth
572		}
573	}

575	// archiveEntryPath normalizes an archive entry name to cleaned, slash-separated
576	// form. Selection and extraction must normalize identically — otherwise the
577	// entry preferredArchiveEntry picked would not match the one extraction
578	// compares against, and the install would fail on an archive that contains the
579	// binary.
580	func archiveEntryPath(name string) string {
581		return path.Clean(filepath.ToSlash(name))
582	}

584	// errNoArchiveEntry reports an archive that holds no usable binary, either
585	// because nothing matched or because the chosen entry vanished between passes.
586	func errNoArchiveEntry(archivePath, binName string) error {
587		return fmt.Errorf("archive %s contains no %s entry", filepath.Base(archivePath), binName)

590	// walkTarGz calls fn for each regular-file entry in a tar.gz, stopping early
591	// when fn returns stop. Both the listing pass and the extraction pass go
592	// through it, so the open/gzip/tar scaffolding exists in one place.
593	func walkTarGz(archivePath string, fn func(hdr *tar.Header, r io.Reader) (stop bool, err error)) error {
594		f, err := os.Open(archivePath) //nolint:gosec // staging-dir file we just wrote
595		if err != nil {
596			return fmt.Errorf("open archive: %w", err)
597		}
598		defer f.Close()
599		gz, err := gzip.NewReader(f)
600		if err != nil {
601			return fmt.Errorf("open gzip: %w", err)
602		}
603		defer gz.Close()
604		tr := tar.NewReader(gz)
605		for {
606			hdr, err := tr.Next()
607			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
608				return nil
609			}
610			if err != nil {
611				return fmt.Errorf("read tar: %w", err)
612			}
613			if hdr.Typeflag != tar.TypeReg {
614				continue
615			}
616			stop, err := fn(hdr, tr)
617			if err != nil {
618				return err
619			}
620			if stop {
621				return nil
622			}
623		}
624	}

626	// selectTarEntry scans a tar.gz and returns the entry extraction should take,
627	// holding one candidate name at a time rather than the whole listing.
628	func selectTarEntry(archivePath, binName string) (string, error) {
629		p := archiveEntryPicker{binName: binName}
630		if err := walkTarGz(archivePath, func(hdr *tar.Header, _ io.Reader) (bool, error) {
631			p.consider(hdr.Name)
632			return false, nil
633		}); err != nil {
634			return "", err
635		}
636		return p.best, nil
637	}

639	func extractFromTarGz(archivePath, binName string, destRoot *os.Root, destName string) error {
640		// Two passes: a tar stream cannot seek backwards, so choosing among
641		// candidates means selecting first and extracting second. The cost is one
642		// extra inflation of an archive already capped at maxPluginAssetSize —
643		// ~100ms on a 50 MiB archive, against a download measured in seconds —
644		// which buys a deterministic choice.
645		want, err := selectTarEntry(archivePath, binName)
646		if err != nil {
647			return err
648		}
649		if want == "" {
650			return errNoArchiveEntry(archivePath, binName)
651		}
652		found := false
653		if err := walkTarGz(archivePath, func(hdr *tar.Header, r io.Reader) (bool, error) {
654			if archiveEntryPath(hdr.Name) != want {
655				return false, nil
656			}
657			found = true
658			return true, writeExecutable(destRoot, destName, r)
659		}); err != nil {
660			return err
661		}
662		if !found {
663			return errNoArchiveEntry(archivePath, binName)
664		}
665		return nil
666	}

668	func extractFromZip(archivePath, binName string, destRoot *os.Root, destName string) error {
669		zr, err := zip.OpenReader(archivePath)
670		if err != nil {
671			return fmt.Errorf("open zip: %w", err)
672		}
673		defer zr.Close()
674		p := archiveEntryPicker{binName: binName}
675		for _, f := range zr.File {
676			if !f.FileInfo().IsDir() {
677				p.consider(f.Name)
678			}
679		}
680		want := p.best
681		if want == "" {
682			return errNoArchiveEntry(archivePath, binName)
683		}
684		// zip is random-access, so the chosen entry is reachable directly — no
685		// second scan, and no Close deferred inside a loop.
686		i := slices.IndexFunc(zr.File, func(f *zip.File) bool {
687			return !f.FileInfo().IsDir() && archiveEntryPath(f.Name) == want
688		})
689		if i < 0 {
690			return errNoArchiveEntry(archivePath, binName)
691		}
692		rc, err := zr.File[i].Open()
693		if err != nil {
694			return fmt.Errorf("open zip entry: %w", err)
695		}
696		defer rc.Close()
697		return writeExecutable(destRoot, destName, rc)
698	}

700	// fileSHA256 returns the hex SHA-256 of the file at path. Used to record the
701	// installed binary's digest and to re-check it in `plugin doctor`.
702	func fileSHA256(path string) (string, error) {
703		f, err := os.Open(path) //nolint:gosec // path is inside the managed plugin tree
704		if err != nil {
705			return "", fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", filepath.Base(path), err)
706		}
707		defer f.Close()
708		h := sha256.New()
709		if _, err := io.Copy(h, f); err != nil {
710			return "", fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", filepath.Base(path), err)
711		}
712		return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)), nil
713	}

715	// writeExecutable writes r to destPath with the executable bit set, bounded by
716	// maxPluginAssetSize. Explicit chmod (not inherited archive mode) because
717	// zip-built and raw-binary releases routinely lose the bit — the #1
718	// "downloaded plugin doesn't run" failure.
719	func writeExecutable(root *os.Root, destName string, r io.Reader) error {
720		return writeExecutableLimited(root, destName, r, maxPluginAssetSize)
721	}
722	
723	// writeExecutableLimited is writeExecutable with an explicit cap, so the
724	// oversize path is testable without materializing 512 MiB.
725	//
726	// The cap lives here rather than in each caller's io.LimitReader because a
727	// bare LimitReader makes truncation invisible: io.Copy returns a nil error at
728	// the limit, so an archive entry larger than the cap was silently truncated
729	// and installed as the plugin binary with the install reporting success. Worse
730	// since binary_sha256 landed — the digest is computed from the truncated bytes,
731	// so `plugin doctor` would confirm the corrupt binary as intact. Reading one
732	// byte past the cap makes the overflow detectable, mirroring fetchAndVerify.
733	func writeExecutableLimited(root *os.Root, destName string, r io.Reader, limit int64) error {
734		// Write to a sibling temp file and rename into place. Two reasons, both
735		// load-bearing:
736		//
737		//  - O_CREATE without O_EXCL follows a symlink at destName, so a symlink
738		//    planted at pkg/<name>/entire-<name> by an earlier malicious plugin
739		//    would redirect this write anywhere the user can write (~/.zshrc, a git
740		//    hook). Creating a fresh temp name and renaming cannot follow anything.
741		//    The root is the second, structural half of that: destName resolves
742		//    inside the managed tree, so even a rename target that escaped the
743		//    naming rules cannot land outside it.
744		//  - Opening destPath with O_TRUNC destroys the working binary before the
745		//    new bytes are known-good, so an interrupted or failed copy left the
746		//    plugin broken. This path is the *normal* one whenever staging and the
747		//    managed dir are on different filesystems (a tmpfs /tmp), not an edge
748		//    case.
749		tmp, tmpName, err := jsonutil.CreateTempIn(root, destName)
750		if err != nil {
751			return fmt.Errorf("create staging binary: %w", err)
752		}
753		defer func() { _ = root.Remove(tmpName) }() //nolint:errcheck // no-op once the rename succeeds
754	
755		n, err := io.Copy(tmp, io.LimitReader(r, limit+1))
756		if err != nil {
757			_ = tmp.Close()
758			return fmt.Errorf("write binary: %w", err)
759		}
760		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
761			return fmt.Errorf("close binary: %w", err)
762		}
763		if n > limit {
764			return fmt.Errorf("plugin binary exceeds the %d byte limit", limit)
765		}
766		// CreateTempIn makes 0600; the dispatcher needs it executable.
767		if err := root.Chmod(tmpName, 0o755); err != nil {
768			return fmt.Errorf("set executable bit: %w", err)
769		}
770		if err := root.Rename(tmpName, destName); err != nil {
771			return fmt.Errorf("place binary: %w", err)
772		}
773		return nil
774	}

64	// Dependency resolution deliberately does not happen here — callers
65	// (the install command) plan and confirm dependency installs first.
66	// expectedName is the plugin name the caller has already committed to — the
67	// index entry the user asked for, the requirement being satisfied, or the
68	// plugin being upgraded. Pass "" only for a bare `install <url>`, where the
69	// repository legitimately names itself; installRepoAtTag explains why a
70	// mismatch is otherwise fatal.

73	// field it could be silently omitted, and omitting it reopens a no-prompt
74	// name-substitution hole; as an argument, passing "" is a visible choice at
75	// the call site.
76	func InstallPluginFromRepo(ctx context.Context, repoURL, expectedName string, opts RemoteInstallOptions) (*RemoteInstallResult, error) {
77		repoURL = strings.TrimRight(repoURL, "/")
78	
79		var tags []string
80		if opts.Pin != "" {
81			tags = []string{opts.Pin}
82		} else {
83			var err error
84			stopTags := startPluginStep(ctx, "Finding latest plugin release...")
85			tags, err = listRemoteSemverTags(ctx, repoURL)
86			stopTags()

88				return nil, err

91				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s has no stable semver tags; prereleases are skipped, so pass --pin <tag> to install one (or a non-semver tag)", redactURL(repoURL))
92			}

94				tags = tags[:maxTagFallbacks]

96		}

98		var lastErr error
99		for i, tag := range tags {

101			if err == nil {

103				return res, nil
104			}
105			lastErr = err
106			if !errors.Is(err, errAssetNotFound) {
107				return nil, err
108			}
109		}
110		return nil, lastErr
111	}

113	func installRepoAtTag(ctx context.Context, repoURL, expectedName, tag string, opts RemoteInstallOptions) (*RemoteInstallResult, error) {

115		meta, err := fetchPluginMetadataAtTag(ctx, repoURL, tag)
116		stopMetadata()
117		if err != nil {
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		// The installed name comes from the *remote* — entire-plugin.yml's name:,
121		// else the repo basename.
122		var name string
123		if meta != nil && meta.Name != "" {
124			name = meta.Name
125		} else if name, err = pluginNameFromRepoURL(repoURL); err != nil {
126			return nil, err
127		}
128	
129		// Reconcile it with what the caller asked for. Unchecked, the remote chose
130		// the name unilaterally, which broke three things:
131		//
132		//  - `install <index-name>` could install something else entirely: the
133		//    index entry says "safe", the repo declares "hijack", and the user gets
134		//    entire-hijack on PATH with no prompt (index installs never prompt).
135		//  - --force escalated across plugins: the already-installed check below
136		//    tests the *remote-declared* name, so reinstalling A let A's repo
137		//    declare name: B and replace an unrelated installed B.
138		//  - A dependency installed under a different name never satisfied the
139		//    requirement, so dependencySatisfied/doctor reported it missing forever
140		//    and every future parent install re-attempted it.
141		//
142		// Fatal rather than a warning: every caller that sets ExpectedName has
143		// already made a trust decision about *that* name, and silently honoring a
144		// different one voids it. A legitimate rename is a catalog or requirement
145		// to fix, and the message says so.
146		if expectedName != "" && name != expectedName {
147			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
148				"%s declares plugin name %q but %q was requested; refusing to install under a name that was not asked for (update the plugin index entry or the requirement if the plugin was renamed)",
149				redactURL(repoURL), name, expectedName)
150		}
151	
152		existing, err := FindInstalledPlugin(name)
153		if err != nil {
154			return nil, err
155		}
156		if existing != nil && !opts.Force {
157			return nil, fmt.Errorf("plugin %q already installed at %s; use --force to replace", name, existing.Path)
158		}
159		// Note a --force replace that changes where the plugin comes from. A repo
160		// move is legitimate (entire-sem → entire-graph), which is why this is not
161		// refused — but the caller should be able to tell the user what was
162		// displaced and from where.
163		var replacedFrom string
164		if existing != nil {
165			if prev, prevErr := LoadPluginManifest(name); prevErr == nil && prev != nil &&
166				normalizeRepoURL(prev.RepoURL) != normalizeRepoURL(repoURL) {
167				replacedFrom = prev.RepoURL
168			}
169		}
170	
171		staging, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "entire-plugin-fetch-")
172		if err != nil {
173			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create staging dir: %w", err)
174		}
175		// Best-effort cleanup of our own temp dir. Forget before RemoveAll: the
176		// staging root below is memoized under this path, and a cached root that
177		// outlives its directory is a handle to an unlinked inode — one leaked fd
178		// and one dead registry entry per plugin installed, N per `plugin upgrade`.
179		// plugin_fetch.go opens the same directory, so this one Forget covers both.
180		defer func() {
181			osroot.Forget(staging)
182			_ = os.RemoveAll(staging)
183		}()
184		// The staging directory gets a root too. It holds a downloaded archive and
185		// whatever the extractor pulls out of it, and it is the one place a future
186		// change that honours archive entry names would write.
187		stagingRoot, err := osroot.Shared(staging)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open staging dir: %w", err)
190		}
191	
192		asset, err := downloadPluginAsset(ctx, meta, repoURL, name, tag, staging, opts.AllowUnverified)
193		if err != nil {
194			return nil, err
195		}
196	
197		stopInstall := startPluginStep(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("Installing entire-%s %s...", name, tag))
198		defer stopInstall()
199		binBase := pluginBinaryName(name)
200		stagedName := "extracted-" + binBase
201		if err := extractPluginBinary(asset.Path, name, stagingRoot, stagedName); err != nil {
202			return nil, err
203		}
204	
205		pkgDir, err := EnsurePluginPkgDir(name)
206		if err != nil {
207			return nil, err
208		}
209		pkgName, err := pluginPkgName(name)
210		if err != nil {
211			return nil, err
212		}
213		pluginTreeRoot, err := pluginRoot(true)
214		if err != nil {
215			return nil, err
216		}
217		sweepOldBinaries(pluginTreeRoot, pkgName)
218		pkgBinName := pkgName + "/" + binBase
219		pkgBin := filepath.Join(pkgDir, binBase)
220		if err := replaceBinary(stagingRoot, stagedName, pluginTreeRoot, pkgBinName); err != nil {
221			return nil, fmt.Errorf("place plugin binary: %w", err)
222		}
223	
224		// Digest the binary we actually placed, not just the archive it came from.
225		// asset.SHA256 covers the downloaded asset, which is discarded with the
226		// staging dir — so it records provenance but can never detect later
227		// tampering. binDigest is what `plugin doctor` re-checks.
228		binDigest, err := fileSHA256(pkgBin)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("hash installed plugin binary: %w", err)
231		}
232	
233		manifest := &PluginManifest{
234			Name:         name,
235			RepoURL:      repoURL,
236			Tag:          tag,
237			Asset:        asset.Asset,
238			SHA256:       asset.SHA256,
239			BinarySHA256: binDigest,
240			Unverified:   !asset.Verified,
241			Pinned:       opts.Pin != "",
242			InstalledAt:  time.Now().UTC(),
243		}
244		if meta != nil {
245			manifest.Requires = meta.Requires
246		}
247		// The manifest is written before the bin/ link, immediately after the
248		// binary swap. Ordering matters because replaceBinary has already mutated
249		// pkg/<name>/: until the manifest catches up, it records the *previous*
250		// tag and binary_sha256 while the new binary is on disk, and
251		// checkManagedBinaryIntegrity reads that as tampering — a permanent false
252		// alarm on a perfectly good install. Writing it here leaves only the local
253		// re-hash above in that window.
254		//
255		// If the bin/ link then fails, the manifest is still accurate and doctor
256		// reports the real problem ("has an install manifest but no entry in the
257		// managed bin dir") with a fix that works, instead of accusing the user of
258		// tampering.
259		if err := SavePluginManifest(manifest); err != nil {
260			return nil, err
261		}
262	
263		installed, err := InstallPluginFromPath(InstallPluginOptions{SourcePath: pkgBin, Force: true})
264		if err != nil {
265			return nil, err
266		}
267		return &RemoteInstallResult{Installed: installed, Manifest: manifest, Metadata: meta, ReplacedFrom: replacedFrom}, nil
268	}
269	
270	// UpgradeOutcome describes what UpgradeInstalledPlugin did.
271	type UpgradeOutcome struct {
272		Name string
273		// Pinned: skipped because the manifest is pinned.
274		Pinned bool
275		// UpToDate: already at the newest tag.
276		UpToDate bool
277		// FromTag/ToTag are set when an upgrade actually happened.
278		FromTag, ToTag string
279	}
280	
281	// UpgradeInstalledPlugin re-resolves the newest tag for a remote-installed
282	// plugin and reinstalls when it differs from the manifest's tag. Plugins
283	// without a manifest (local-dev symlinks) are not upgradable.
284	func UpgradeInstalledPlugin(ctx context.Context, name string) (*UpgradeOutcome, error) {
285		m, err := LoadPluginManifest(name)
286		if err != nil {
287			return nil, err
288		}
289		if m == nil {
290			return nil, fmt.Errorf("plugin %q has no install manifest (local-dev install?); reinstall it from its repository URL to make it upgradable", name)
291		}
292		if m.Pinned {
293			return &UpgradeOutcome{Name: name, Pinned: true}, nil
294		}
295		tags, err := listRemoteSemverTags(ctx, m.RepoURL)
296		if err != nil {
297			return nil, err
298		}
299		if len(tags) == 0 {
300			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s has no stable semver tags; prereleases are skipped, so pass --pin <tag> to move to one", redactURL(m.RepoURL))
301		}
302		// Semver comparison, not string equality: "v0.2.0" and "0.2.0" are the
303		// same version, and a remote that re-tagged with the other spelling
304		// must not trigger a reinstall.
305		if semver.Compare(canonicalSemver(tags[0]), canonicalSemver(m.Tag)) <= 0 {
306			return &UpgradeOutcome{Name: name, UpToDate: true}, nil
307		}
308		// Inherit the install-time trust decision: a plugin the user knowingly
309		// installed unverified shouldn't start failing on upgrade, and one
310		// installed verified must not silently downgrade to unverified.
311		res, err := InstallPluginFromRepo(ctx, m.RepoURL, name, RemoteInstallOptions{
312			Force: true, AllowUnverified: m.Unverified,
313		})
314		if err != nil {
315			return nil, err
316		}
317		// The install may have fallen back past an asset-less newest tag and
318		// landed on the version already installed — that's up-to-date, not an
319		// upgrade line claiming X → X.
320		if semver.Compare(canonicalSemver(res.Manifest.Tag), canonicalSemver(m.Tag)) <= 0 {
321			return &UpgradeOutcome{Name: name, UpToDate: true}, nil
322		}
323		return &UpgradeOutcome{Name: name, FromTag: m.Tag, ToTag: res.Manifest.Tag}, nil
324	}
325	
326	// replaceBinary moves src over dest atomically. On Windows, a running
327	// executable can't be replaced (sharing violation) but it *can* be renamed:
328	// move the old binary aside to a .old-<rand> file and retry; leftovers are
329	// swept on the next install. os.Rename fails across filesystems (staging is
330	// in the system temp dir), so a copy fallback covers that case.
331	// srcName is a name inside srcRoot (the staging dir); destName a name inside
332	// destRoot (the managed tree). The two are separate roots because staging is in
333	// the system temp dir, which is also why the cross-device copy fallback exists.
334	func replaceBinary(srcRoot *os.Root, srcName string, destRoot *os.Root, destName string) error {
335		// os.Rename across two roots has no root-scoped form, so the cross-root move
336		// uses absolute paths built from each root's own name. Both halves are still
337		// resolved through their roots for every other operation, and the copy
338		// fallback below — the path that actually runs whenever /tmp is a different
339		// filesystem — is fully rooted on both sides.
340		src := filepath.Join(srcRoot.Name(), filepath.FromSlash(srcName))
341		dest := filepath.Join(destRoot.Name(), filepath.FromSlash(destName))
342		err := os.Rename(src, dest)
343		if err == nil {
344			return nil
345		}
346		if runtime.GOOS == windowsGOOS {
347			if asideErr := destRoot.Rename(destName, oldBinaryAsideName(destName)); asideErr == nil {
348				if err = os.Rename(src, dest); err == nil {
349					return nil
350				}
351			}
352		}
353		// Cross-device rename: copy + fsync-free write, then remove src.
354		in, openErr := srcRoot.Open(srcName)
355		if openErr != nil {
356			return errors.Join(err, openErr)
357		}
358		defer in.Close()
359		if writeErr := writeExecutable(destRoot, destName, in); writeErr != nil {
360			return errors.Join(err, writeErr)
361		}
362		_ = srcRoot.Remove(srcName) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup of our own staging file
363		return nil
364	}
365	
366	// oldBinaryAsideName returns a unique .old- sibling name for the rename-aside
367	// trick. Random suffix so concurrent upgrades can't collide.
368	func oldBinaryAsideName(destName string) string {
369		var b [4]byte
370		if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
371			return destName + ".old-fallback"
372		}
373		return destName + ".old-" + hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
374	}
375	
376	// sweepOldBinaries best-effort removes .old-* leftovers from the Windows
377	// rename-aside fallback. Failures are ignored — the files are inert.
378	func sweepOldBinaries(root *os.Root, pkgName string) {
379		entries, err := osroot.ReadDirNoSymlinks(root, pkgName)
380		if err != nil {
381			return
382		}
383		for _, e := range entries {
384			if strings.Contains(e.Name(), ".old-") {
385				_ = root.Remove(pkgName + "/" + e.Name()) //nolint:errcheck // inert leftovers; swept again next install
386			}
387		}
388	}
389	
390	// RemoveManagedPlugin removes a plugin's bin entries and its pkg dir.
391	// The dependency guard lives in the command layer so --force can bypass it.
392	func RemoveManagedPlugin(name string) error {
393		if err := RemoveInstalledPlugin(name); err != nil {
394			return err
395		}
396		return RemovePluginPkg(name)
397	}

1	package jsonutil
2	
3	import (
4		"crypto/rand"
5		"encoding/hex"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io/fs"
9		"os"
10		"path"

16	
17	// WriteFileAtomic writes data to filePath atomically by writing to a temp file
18	// in the same directory and renaming it into place. A crash or signal mid-write
19	// leaves the original file intact rather than a truncated partial — important
20	// for config files like .entire/settings.json that callers expect to remain
21	// parseable across interrupted writes.
22	//
23	// The rename is what provides that, and it is deliberately NOT paired with an
24	// fsync. The property every caller here needs is "a reader never sees a torn
25	// file", which the rename gives on its own. fsync buys something different —
26	// that the bytes survive a power loss — and nothing written through this
27	// function is worth that price: settings, session state, caches and manifests
28	// are all reconstructible, and losing the last write to one costs a repeated
29	// command, not data. The price is not small, measured at 14x on a 4KiB payload
30	// (1.02ms against 71µs), and session state is written on every agent hook.
31	//
32	// What is given up, precisely: on a filesystem that reorders the rename ahead
33	// of the data write, a hard power loss can leave a zero-length file where the
34	// old contents used to be. Every reader here treats an unparseable or empty
35	// file as absent and rebuilds it.
36	//
37	// perm is applied to the temp file via Chmod before rename so the final file
38	// lands with the requested permission regardless of the temp file's default.
39	func WriteFileAtomic(filePath string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error {
40		dir := filepath.Dir(filePath)
41		base := filepath.Base(filePath)
42		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, base+".*.tmp")
43		if err != nil {
44			return fmt.Errorf("create temp for %s: %w", filePath, err)
45		}
46		tmpName := tmp.Name()
47		removeTmp := true
48		defer func() {
49			if removeTmp {
50				_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
51			}
52		}()
53		if _, err := tmp.Write(data); err != nil {
54			_ = tmp.Close()
55			return fmt.Errorf("write temp for %s: %w", filePath, err)
56		}
57		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
58			return fmt.Errorf("close temp for %s: %w", filePath, err)
59		}
60		if err := os.Chmod(tmpName, perm); err != nil {
61			return fmt.Errorf("chmod temp for %s: %w", filePath, err)
62		}
63		if err := os.Rename(tmpName, filePath); err != nil {
64			return fmt.Errorf("rename temp to %s: %w", filePath, err)
65		}
66		removeTmp = false
67		return nil
68	}

70	// WriteFileAtomicIn is WriteFileAtomic confined to root: name is resolved
71	// relative to root by the kernel, so neither the temp file nor the rename
72	// target can escape it. It is the form every .entire writer uses, because the
73	// names under .entire are built from agent-supplied session and tool-use IDs.
74	//
75	// The sequence is identical to WriteFileAtomic — write, close, chmod, rename,
76	// and no fsync — and the same reasoning applies to each step. Two differences:
77	// os.Root has no CreateTemp, so the unique temp name is drawn here and created
78	// with O_EXCL (a collision retries rather than clobbering a concurrent writer's
79	// temp file); and the parent directory is opened once, up front, with every
80	// component checked for symlinks, so the temp file, the chmod and the rename
81	// all act on the same pinned directory rather than re-resolving name each time.
82	//
83	// name must be a valid slash-separated path beneath root (see fs.ValidPath):
84	// "./x", "x//y" and "x/./y" are rejected rather than cleaned.
85	func WriteFileAtomicIn(root *os.Root, name string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error {
86		parent, leaf, closeParent, err := osroot.OpenParentNoSymlinks(root, name)
87		if err != nil {
88			return fmt.Errorf("open parent for %s: %w", name, err)
89		}
90		defer closeParent()
91	
92		tmp, tmpName, err := CreateTempIn(parent, leaf)
93		if err != nil {
94			return fmt.Errorf("create temp for %s: %w", name, err)
95		}
96		removeTmp := true
97		defer func() {
98			if removeTmp {
99				_ = parent.Remove(tmpName) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup of a temp file the rename did not consume
100			}
101		}()
102		if _, err := tmp.Write(data); err != nil {
103			_ = tmp.Close()
104			return fmt.Errorf("write temp for %s: %w", name, err)
105		}
106		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
107			return fmt.Errorf("close temp for %s: %w", name, err)
108		}
109		if err := parent.Chmod(tmpName, perm); err != nil {
110			return fmt.Errorf("chmod temp for %s: %w", name, err)
111		}

125	// tempRandomHexLen is the length of the random component CreateTempIn inserts,
126	// in hex characters: 8 bytes, so 16.
127	const tempRandomHexLen = 16

129	// IsTempName reports whether name was produced by CreateTempIn.
130	//
131	// It exists because an atomic write leaves its temp file in the SAME directory
132	// as its target, and one of those directories — .entire/metadata/<session> — is
133	// walked wholesale into every checkpoint tree. A hook killed between
134	// CreateTempIn and Rename (an agent's hook timeout, Codex's session-end process
135	// tree kill, a crash) leaves the temp behind, and without this the walk redacts
136	// it, commits it, and pushes it on every checkpoint from then on.
137	//
138	// The match is the whole shape CreateTempIn produces — "<base>.<16 hex>.tmp" —
139	// not a bare ".tmp" suffix, so a file a user or an agent legitimately named
140	// something.tmp is still captured.
141	func IsTempName(name string) bool {
142		base := path.Base(name)
143		rest, ok := strings.CutSuffix(base, tempSuffix)
144		if !ok {
145			return false
146		}
147		dot := strings.LastIndexByte(rest, '.')
148		if dot < 0 {
149			return false
150		}
151		hexPart := rest[dot+1:]
152		if len(hexPart) != tempRandomHexLen {
153			return false
154		}
155		for i := range len(hexPart) {
156			if !isHexDigit(hexPart[i]) {

158			}
159		}

161		// base it was given, so an empty base means this is not one of ours.
162		return dot > 0

165	func isHexDigit(c byte) bool {
166		return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')

170	// name inside root, and returns it with its root-relative name. It is the
171	// os.Root counterpart to os.CreateTemp, which has no Root form.
172	//
173	// O_EXCL rather than a fixed "<name>.tmp": concurrent hook processes write the
174	// same session and checkpoint files, and a shared temp path corrupts whichever
175	// write lands second.
176	func CreateTempIn(root *os.Root, name string) (*os.File, string, error) {
177		dir, base := path.Split(name)
178		var buf [8]byte
179		for range tempNameAttempts {
180			if _, err := rand.Read(buf[:]); err != nil {
181				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("read random suffix: %w", err)
182			}
183			candidate := dir + base + "." + hex.EncodeToString(buf[:]) + tempSuffix
184			f, err := root.OpenFile(candidate, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
185			if err == nil {
186				return f, candidate, nil
187			}
188			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrExist) {
189				return nil, "", err //nolint:wrapcheck // caller names the file; the os error carries op and path
190			}
191		}
192		return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("exhausted %d temp name attempts for %s", tempNameAttempts, name)
193	}

128	// PluginRequirement declares a dependency on another plugin. Shared between
129	// the author-side metadata file (entire-plugin.yml) and the install-side
130	// manifest so the two can never drift.

133	// through the plugin index, so the URL a dependency install fetches from always
134	// comes from the curated catalog rather than from the requiring plugin's author.
135	// With an author-supplied URL, installing one plugin meant fetching and
136	// executing a binary from a URL its author chose — and dependency planning
137	// contacted that URL *before* the confirmation prompt. The capability is not
138	// gone, the authority moved: a user can still install an out-of-catalog
139	// dependency by URL themselves, with the usual untrusted-source prompt, after

173	// file at the root of a plugin repository.

176	// ParsePluginMetadata decodes entire-plugin.yml content.
177	//
178	// Decoding is lenient: unknown keys are ignored, matching the choice made for
179	// index.json. Both are artifacts read by every CLI version ever shipped, and
180	// refusing one an older binary doesn't fully understand breaks it permanently
181	// for everyone on that version — the plugin author cannot fix it for them.
182	// entire-plugin.yml has no version field to gate on either, so the first author
183	// to adopt any future field (min_cli_version, bin_name, …) would break installs
184	// on every older CLI.
185	//
186	// This deliberately gives up catching author typos here, which strict decoding
187	// did. The trade is asymmetric: a misspelled key costs the author one confused
188	// test run against their own plugin, while a forward-compatibility break is
189	// unfixable and fleet-wide. Author-side validation belongs in a lint command,
190	// not in the hot path every user's install runs through.
191	func ParsePluginMetadata(data []byte) (*PluginMetadata, error) {
192		var meta PluginMetadata
193		dec := yaml.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
194		if err := dec.Decode(&meta); err != nil {
195			// An empty or comment-only stream decodes to io.EOF. The file is
196			// documented as optional and a *missing* one is fine, so a committed
197			// placeholder must not be fatal at every tag. An explicit "---" already
198			// behaved this way; align the empty cases with it.
199			if !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
200				return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing %s: %w", pluginMetadataFileName, err)
201			}
202			meta = PluginMetadata{}
203		}
204		if meta.Name != "" {

207			}
208		}
209		for _, req := range meta.Requires {

211				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s declares invalid requirement: %w", pluginMetadataFileName, err)
212			}
213			// A malformed min_version silently removes the floor rather than
214			// failing: x/mod/semver ranks an invalid string below every valid one,
215			// so semver.Compare(installedTag, garbage) >= 0 is always true and
216			// dependencySatisfied reports any version as acceptable. "vtypo",
217			// "latest" and ">=1.0" all behave that way.
218			//
219			// Rejecting this is consistent with the lenient decoding above, not in
220			// tension with it. Unknown *keys* stay lenient because they are a newer
221			// CLI's fields and refusing them breaks older binaries permanently. A
222			// malformed *value of a known field* is an author error that no CLI
223			// version will ever accept — which is why req.Name is already validated
224			// right here.
225			if req.MinVersion != "" && !semver.IsValid(canonicalSemver(req.MinVersion)) {
226				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s requirement %q declares invalid min_version %q: want a semver tag such as v0.2.0 (a minimum only — ranges are not supported)",

228			}
229		}

268	func LoadPluginManifest(name string) (*PluginManifest, error) {
269		pkgName, err := pluginPkgName(name)

272		}

274		if err != nil {

284			}

286		}

288		if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &m); err != nil {
289			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse plugin manifest for %q: %w", name, err)
290		}
291		return &m, nil
292	}

294	// SavePluginManifest writes the manifest into the plugin's pkg dir.
295	func SavePluginManifest(m *PluginManifest) error {
296		// Strip any credentials before persisting: manifest.yml is mode 0644 and a
297		// token in a remote URL has no business on disk. Upgrades re-resolve the
298		// remote through git's credential helpers, which is where auth belongs.
299		m.RepoURL = redactURL(m.RepoURL)
300		dir, err := EnsurePluginPkgDir(m.Name)
301		if err != nil {
302			return err
303		}
304		data, err := yaml.Marshal(m)
305		if err != nil {
306			return fmt.Errorf("marshal plugin manifest: %w", err)
307		}
308		// Atomic via the shared helper: a torn manifest would read as either a
309		// missing install or a digest mismatch, and this write happens moments
310		// after the binary it describes was swapped in.
311		path := filepath.Join(dir, pluginManifestFileName)
312		if err := jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
313			return fmt.Errorf("write plugin manifest: %w", err)
314		}
315		return nil
316	}

318	// ListPluginManifests returns the manifests of every remote-installed
319	// plugin, sorted by name. Pkg entries without a readable manifest are
320	// skipped — a half-removed plugin shouldn't break listing.
321	func ListPluginManifests() ([]*PluginManifest, error) {
322		parent, err := pluginParentDir()
323		if err != nil {
324			return nil, err
325		}
326		_ = parent // resolved above so a broken plugin dir still reports one error
327		root, err := pluginRoot(false)
328		if err != nil {
329			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
330				return nil, nil
331			}
332			return nil, err
333		}
334		entries, err := osroot.ReadDirNoSymlinks(root, pluginManagedPkgSubdir)
335		if err != nil {
336			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
337				return nil, nil
338			}
339			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read plugin pkg dir: %w", err)
340		}
341		var out []*PluginManifest
342		for _, e := range entries {
343			if !e.IsDir() {
344				continue
345			}
346			m, err := LoadPluginManifest(e.Name())
347			if err != nil || m == nil {
348				continue
349			}
350			out = append(out, m)
351		}
352		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
353		return out, nil
354	}
355	
356	// RemovePluginPkg deletes the plugin's pkg dir (binary + manifest).
357	// Missing dir is not an error — local-dev installs never had one.
358	func RemovePluginPkg(name string) error {
359		name, err := pluginPkgName(name)
360		if err != nil {
361			return err
362		}
363		root, err := pluginRoot(false)
364		if err != nil {
365			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
366				return nil // nothing to remove
367			}
368			return err
369		}
370		if err := root.RemoveAll(name); err != nil {
371			return fmt.Errorf("remove plugin pkg dir: %w", err)
372		}
373		return nil
374	}

20		// unreachable through PATH — a managed bin dir that could not be

40			// with a released binary is their call to make, not ours.
41			if reinstallFixes, cerr := checkManagedPluginRunnable(installed.Path); cerr != nil {
42				broken := fmt.Errorf("the entire-%s plugin is installed at %s but cannot be run: %w", name, installed.Path, cerr)
43				if !reinstallFixes {
44					return "", broken
45				}
46				return "", fmt.Errorf("%w; reinstall it with 'entire plugin install %s --force'", broken, name)
47			}
48			return installed.Path, nil
49		}
50		if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
51			return "", fmt.Errorf("the entire-%s plugin is not installed; run 'entire plugin install %s' and retry", name, name)
52		}
53		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
54			return "", fmt.Errorf("install plugin: %w", err)
55		}
56	
57		// Resolve the source before asking, for two reasons.
58		//
59		// The prompt is the only human checkpoint on this path — an index-listed
60		// install never prompts inside runRemoteInstall, because the catalog is
61		// the trust decision — so it has to say where the binary comes from.
62		// confirmInstallOrCancel names redactURL(repoURL) for an unlisted
63		// repository; a prompt that defaults to Yes and names nothing tells the
64		// user less about a download-and-exec than the one that defaults to No.
65		//
66		// And a name the index does not carry cannot be installed at all, so
67		// asking first and failing afterwards spends the user's Yes on a question
68		// that never had an answer — the same prompt-then-dead-end shape as the
69		// already-installed case above.
70		//
71		// This is not an extra round-trip: SyncPluginIndex touches a freshness
72		// marker, and runRemoteInstall's own call moments later reads the clone
73		// without fetching (pluginIndexTTL). Progress is reported and stopped
74		// before the prompt, per the rule that a spinner never overlaps a
75		// confirmation.
76		indexURL := resolvePluginIndexURL("")
77		stopIndex := startPluginStep(withPluginProgress(ctx, rootCmd.ErrOrStderr()), "Checking plugin index...")
78		idx, err := SyncPluginIndex(ctx, indexURL, false)
79		stopIndex()
80		if err != nil {
81			return "", fmt.Errorf("look up the entire-%s plugin in the plugin index %s: %w", name, redactURL(indexURL), err)
82		}
83		entry := idx.Find(name)
84		if entry == nil {
85			return "", fmt.Errorf("the entire-%s plugin is not listed in the plugin index %s, so it cannot be installed on demand; install it from its repository URL with 'entire plugin install <url>'", name, redactURL(indexURL))
86		}
87	
88		confirmed, err := runPluginConfirm(ctx, rootCmd.ErrOrStderr(),
89			fmt.Sprintf("Install the entire-%s plugin from %s?", name, redactURL(entry.RepoURL)), true)
90		if err != nil {
91			if ctx.Err() != nil {
92				return "", err
93			}
94			return "", handleFormCancellation(rootCmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Install", err)
95		}
96		if !confirmed {
97			fmt.Fprintln(rootCmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Install cancelled.")
98			return "", nil
99		}
100		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
101			return "", fmt.Errorf("install plugin: %w", err)
102		}
103	
104		// Keep install progress off stdout: the original command may emit JSON or
105		// be piped to another tool. Do not parse any of the plugin's arguments.
106		cmd := newPluginInstallCmd()
107		cmd.SetOut(rootCmd.ErrOrStderr())
108		cmd.SetErr(rootCmd.ErrOrStderr())
109		// Resolved carries the entry the prompt named, so the install cannot
110		// re-resolve into a different repository after the user has agreed to
111		// this one — see installSource.Resolved.
112		src := installSource{Kind: installFromIndex, Ref: name, Resolved: entry}
113		if err := onDemandPluginInstall(ctx, cmd, src, remoteInstallFlags{}); err != nil {
114			return "", err
115		}
116		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
117			return "", fmt.Errorf("install plugin: %w", err)
118		}
119		installed, err := FindInstalledPlugin(name)
120		if err != nil {
121			return "", err
122		}
123		if installed == nil {
124			return "", fmt.Errorf("the entire-%s plugin was not installed; run 'entire plugin install %s' and retry", name, name)
125		}
126		// Execute the managed entry directly, even if the managed directory could
127		// not be prepended to PATH at startup.
128		return installed.Path, nil
129	}

131	// checkManagedPluginRunnable reports why a managed plugin entry cannot be
132	// executed, or a nil error when it can. reinstallFixes is true only for a
133	// condition a reinstall actually repairs, so the caller does not attach that
134	// remedy to an error it would not resolve — a permission failure on the
135	// managed directory is not fixed by installing into it, and a remedy hung off
136	// an unmatched error is how advice comes to name the wrong cause (the mistake
137	// writeEntireDirRemedy documents for `.entire`). It is meaningless when the
138	// error is nil.
139	//
140	// os.Stat rather than Lstat, deliberately: the question is whether the thing
141	// at the end of the entry exists, and a dangling symlink is the case that
142	// brought this function into being. The executable bit is left to the exec —
143	// findInaccessiblePlugin draws the same line for PATH entries, and the mode
144	// does not mean the same thing on Windows.
145	func checkManagedPluginRunnable(path string) (reinstallFixes bool, err error) {
146		info, statErr := os.Stat(path)
147		if statErr != nil {
148			if errors.Is(statErr, os.ErrNotExist) {
149				// Worded rather than passed through because the errno itself ("no
150				// such file or directory") describes the entry, which plainly
151				// exists; what is missing is whatever it points at.
152				return true, errors.New("it points at a file that no longer exists")
153			}
154			return false, statErr //nolint:wrapcheck // the caller adds the plugin name and path
155		}
156		if info.IsDir() {
157			return true, errors.New("it is a directory")
158		}
159		return false, nil
160	}

24	func main() {

26		versioninfo.Load()

28		// Create context that cancels on interrupt
29		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
30	
31		// Memoize this process's .git/config remote reads. The checkpoint sync
32		// election re-runs per call by design and each run shells out to git for the
33		// same two answers; one command can elect several times. Answers are
34		// partitioned per git working directory, so a command walking several repos
35		// stays correct. `entire repo mirror use` invalidates after re-pointing a
36		// remote, and `entire mcp` narrows this to one window per request.
37		ctx = strategy.WithGitRemoteCache(ctx)

39		// Handle interrupt signals
40		sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
41		signals := []os.Signal{os.Interrupt}
42		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
43			signals = append(signals, syscall.SIGTERM)
44		}
45		signal.Notify(sigChan, signals...)
46		go func() {

48			// cleanly. signal.Notify has disabled Go's default "signal
49			// terminates" behavior, so without the second read below a user
50			// who Ctrl-C's again during a slow/stuck shutdown (e.g. a keyring
51			// read blocked in a subprocess we can't cancel) would find every
52			// further Ctrl-C swallowed. The second read restores an escape
53			// hatch: signal again to force-exit.
54			//

56			// re-raises that same signal — a SIGTERM (from a supervisor /
57			// container stop) must exit 143, not masquerade as a SIGINT 130.
58			sig := <-sigChan
59			procsignal.Store(sig)
60			if sig == os.Interrupt {
61				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nInterrupting… press Ctrl-C again to force quit.")
62			} else {
63				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nReceived termination signal, shutting down… signal again to force quit.")
64			}
65			cancel()
66			<-sigChan
67			dieFromSignal(sig)

70		// Create and execute root command
71		rootCmd := cli.NewRootCmd()

74		// dispatcher: prepend the managed bin dir to PATH before resolution.
75		// Idempotent and silent on failure (managed installs simply won't be
76		// found this run; PATH-installed plugins still work). The closure
77		// restores PATH so built-in commands and their subprocesses don't
78		// inherit the prepended dir. When a plugin runs, we skip the restore
79		// — the os.Exit ends the process, and the plugin child intentionally
80		// inherits the prepended PATH so it can spawn sibling managed plugins.
81		restorePATH := cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH(ctx)

83		if handled, code, killedBy := cli.MaybeRunPlugin(ctx, rootCmd, os.Args[1:]); handled {

87				// the on-demand install before it ran. Re-raise so the shell sees
88				// WIFSIGNALED: an enclosing loop breaks on one Ctrl-C, and the
89				// conventional 128+signum reaches whoever ran us.
90				//
91				// Gated on the plugin's own outcome rather than on a signal
92				// having fired somewhere in this process: Ctrl-C reaches the whole
93				// foreground process group, so a plugin that handles it itself and
94				// exits with a meaningful code (a TUI quitting on Ctrl-C exits 0)

97				case procsignal.Load() != nil:
98					// A signal we received outranks the child's, because when we
99					// were signalled the child's signal is usually OUR signal
100					// laundered — and laundered lossily. Cancelling the context
101					// makes runPlugin's cmd.Cancel send the child SIGINT whatever
102					// we got, so a supervisor's SIGTERM comes back as a SIGINT
103					// child and would report 130 for a shutdown that must report
104					// 143. That is the exact confusion dieFromSignal exists to
105					// prevent.
106					dieFromSignal(terminatingSignal())
107				case killedBy != nil:
108					// We were not signalled, so the child's signal is genuinely
109					// its own: `kill -TERM` aimed at the plugin still exits 143,
110					// and a SIGPIPE from `entire graph | head -1` still exits

112					// propagate.

116					// child as an ordinary exit code, so it never lands here;
117					// anything that does is unaccounted for, and -1 is not an
118					// exit status (os.Exit would truncate it to 255), so report a
119					// plain failure rather than inventing a signal.

126	
127		// Retired env vars fail every built-in command up front; a removed knob
128		// must never be silently ignored. Plugins (above) are exempt — what they
129		// read is their business.
130		if err := api.RejectRemovedAuthEnv(); err != nil {
131			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
132			cancel()
133			os.Exit(1)
134		}

136		executed, err := rootCmd.ExecuteContextC(ctx)
137		// The only place the logger is closed, and it must be here: cobra returns out
138		// of Command.execute() as soon as RunE errors or required-flag validation
139		// fails, both before its PersistentPostRun loop, so those paths would
140		// otherwise exit with up to 8KB of buffered diagnostics unwritten. The logger
141		// rides the executed command's context, where the root pre-run put it; a
142		// failure raised before any pre-run carries none, and nothing logged yet.

178				// cobra.ExactArgs) and surface as "accepts N arg(s), received M".

180				// actually expects — rootCmd's usage isn't useful for a
181				// subcommand-level arg mismatch. ExecuteContextC returns the

185				// The choke point for everything a command returns rather than
186				// prints itself: see cli.RenderUserFacingError for what it strips
187				// and which other render sites exist.
188				fmt.Fprintln(rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), cli.RenderUserFacingError(err))

192			os.Exit(1)
193		}
194		if cli.ShouldCheckCheckpointPolicyWarning(executed) {
195			cli.WarnCheckpointPolicyIfNeeded(ctx, rootCmd.ErrOrStderr(), versioninfo.Version)
196		}

200	// terminatingSignal returns the signal that cancelled the root context,
201	// defaulting to SIGINT when the cancellation came from something other than a
202	// recorded terminating signal (so a stray context.Canceled still exits 130).
203	// The recorded signal lives in the shared procsignal package, written by the
204	// handler goroutine (SIGINT/SIGTERM) and by the keyring interrupt path (SIGINT).
205	func terminatingSignal() os.Signal {
206		if s := procsignal.Load(); s != nil {
207			return s
208		}
209		return os.Interrupt
210	}
211	
212	// dieFromSignal terminates the process as if it had been killed by sig, rather
213	// than exiting normally. The distinction matters to an interactive shell: it
214	// only aborts a `while true; do entire ...; done` loop when the child is
215	// *killed by* SIGINT (WIFSIGNALED). A plain os.Exit(130) is an ordinary exit,
216	// so the loop keeps respawning entire and Ctrl-C never escapes it. Re-raising
217	// the actual signal also keeps a SIGTERM shutdown reporting the conventional
218	// 143 (not 130). We reset sig to its default disposition, re-raise it to
219	// ourselves, and briefly wait for delivery; if the re-raise can't be delivered
220	// (e.g. Windows, where signal-to-self is unsupported) we fall back to a
221	// conventional 128+signal exit so we never hang.
222	func dieFromSignal(sig os.Signal) {
223		signal.Reset(sig)
224		if p, err := os.FindProcess(os.Getpid()); err == nil {
225			if err := p.Signal(sig); err == nil {
226				time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) // signal delivery ends the process well before this elapses
227			}
228		}
229		os.Exit(exitCodeForSignal(sig))
230	}
231	
232	// exitCodeForSignal maps a signal to the conventional 128+signum exit code
233	// (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM), falling back to 130 for a signal that
234	// doesn't carry a numeric value on this platform.
235	func exitCodeForSignal(sig os.Signal) int {
236		if s, ok := sig.(syscall.Signal); ok {
237			return 128 + int(s)
238		}
239		return 130
240	}
241	
242	// isPositionalArgError reports whether err looks like a cobra positional-
243	// arg validator failure. cobra's stock validators (ExactArgs, NoArgs,
244	// MinimumNArgs, MaximumNArgs, RangeArgs) all surface error strings
245	// containing "arg(s)", and that substring doesn't appear in cobra's other
246	// error paths or in the cli's own errors — so it's a stable, cheap
247	// discriminator without reaching into cobra internals.
248	func isPositionalArgError(err error) bool {
249		return strings.Contains(err.Error(), "arg(s)")
250	}

252	func showSuggestion(cmd *cobra.Command, err error) {
253		// Print usage first (brew style)
254		fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStderr(), cmd.UsageString())
255		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStderr(), "\nError: Invalid usage: %v\n", err)
256	}

59	// postPluginVersionCheck is a test seam for the version-check notice that

63	// MaybeRunPlugin returns (true, exitCode) when an external command was
64	// resolved and run. On launch failure (e.g. missing executable bit)
65	// returns (true, 1) after printing to stderr. On no-match returns
66	// (false, 0) so the caller can fall through to Cobra. exitCode is
67	// ExitPluginSignalled when the plugin was killed by a signal, or when a
68	// signal interrupted an on-demand install before it ran; the caller turns
69	// that into a re-raised signal rather than an exit status.

72	// one. It is nil for an ordinary exit, on Windows, and for an install
73	// interrupted before any child existed — in that last case the signal is the
74	// one this process received, which the caller already has.
75	//
76	// Telemetry and the version-check notice mirror Cobra's PersistentPostRun
77	// behavior for built-ins: both fire only on a successful (exit-0) run.
78	func MaybeRunPlugin(ctx context.Context, rootCmd *cobra.Command, args []string) (handled bool, exitCode int, killedBy os.Signal) {
79		binPath, pluginArgs, ok := resolvePlugin(rootCmd, args)
80		if !ok {

94					// caller falls back to the one it received.

112			// repositions the cursor or repaints what is above it. That last one

276				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
277		}

282			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {

content.content:
A `graph` that is already in the [managed install directory](#managed-install-directory) but unreachable through `$PATH` — a managed dir that could not be prepended at startup — is **executed**, not offered for installation. Installing over it cannot work: an existing install needs `--force`, which the on-demand path deliberately does not pass, so prompting would spend the user's Yes and several network round-trips on a guaranteed "already installed; use --force to replace".

   A managed entry that exists but **cannot be run** — a local-dev symlink whose target moved, or a directory in its place — is reported with its path and a `entire plugin install <name> --force` remedy. It is neither executed (a `fork/exec` ENOENT names a path the user never chose) nor reinstalled over: replacing a developer's deliberate symlink with a released binary is their call.

### Managed install directory

Users can drop binaries anywhere on `$PATH`, but a per-user managed directory is also automatically discovered:

- **Default:** `$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins/bin` (Linux/macOS) or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\entire\plugins\bin` (Windows).
- **Override:** `$ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR/bin`.

The CLI prepends this directory to `$PATH` at startup via `cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH()` so the existing `exec.LookPath` resolution finds managed installs without any special-casing. This is purely additive — the kubectl-style `$PATH` model is unchanged.

`entire plugin install/list/remove/upgrade` manage the contents of this directory. Authors who prefer the raw "drop a binary on `$PATH`" model don't need to use it.

### Install progress and confirmations

`entire plugin install`, `entire plugin upgrade`, dependency installs, and the on-demand `entire graph` install report their stages — index lookup, release metadata, download and checksum verification, placement — on **stderr**, so stdout carries only the result and stays pipeable. A styled terminal gets a spinner; a non-terminal writer and accessibility mode get one plain line per stage as it starts. Progress stops before any confirmation or result is printed, including on failure. Asset-name probing shares one download status per release rather than one per candidate.

Progress travels on the context (`withPluginProgress`), so a caller that has not opted in prints nothing — a library caller never writes to the process's terminal on its own.

Confirmations read from the **controlling terminal**, never stdin, so a plugin's piped input survives being prompted about. They render to the writer the caller supplies, except when that writer is not itself a terminal (`entire graph 2>log`): then the prompt renders on the terminal the answer is read from, because a prompt nobody can see still blocks on a keypress — and with Yes as the default, an unwitting Enter would authorize the install. An input that reaches EOF never becomes a Yes, but the two modes get there differently: accessibility mode declines outright — huh's scanner would otherwise read EOF as the field's default, which is Yes here — while the default full-screen prompt keeps waiting until the context is cancelled. Both fail closed; only one of them answers. Cancellation stops the prompt either way, and still terminates by signal.

### Remote install

`entire plugin install` accepts three source forms:

| Form | Example | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| bare name | `entire plugin install run` | Resolved through the [plugin index](#plugin-index-discovery) |
| repository URL | `entire plugin install https://github.com/entireio/entire-run` | Installs from any git host. Also accepts git's scp-like form with any SSH username (`deploy@git.corp.io:group/entire-foo.git`) — the same set `validatePluginRepoURL` allows |
| local path | `entire plugin install ./dist/entire-run` | Symlink/copy into the managed dir (unchanged) |

Remote installs are deliberately forge-agnostic:

1. **Version resolution** uses `git ls-remote --tags` — identical on GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, and self-hosted servers; inherits the user's git auth and proxy config. The highest **stable** semver tag wins; `--pin <tag>` installs exactly that tag and marks the manifest pinned (skipped by `upgrade`).

   Prereleases are excluded from resolution. semver ranks `v2.0.0-rc1` above stable `v1.9.0`, so listing them would move every user onto a release candidate on the next `plugin upgrade --all` the moment an author pushed one. `--pin` is the opt-in, since it bypasses listing entirely. Every git subprocess also carries a two-minute deadline — the root context is cancellable but has no timeout, so an unreachable host would otherwise hang the command with no output, which matters most during dependency planning against author-controlled URLs.
